Subject: Severe p99 spikes + 429 cascade on fhir-batch during morning window

Evelyn —

We're seeing a sudden, repeatable regression in tail latency and a wave of 429s starting ~09:45 PT this morning across our nightly fhir-batch ingestion. p50 looked fine, p95 jumped from ~300ms to ~2.1s and p99s spiked to 6–8s. Concurrently our client started receiving 429s which triggered our retry logic and created a retry cascade — clients reissued many concurrent requests and started hitting timeouts. The downstream effect is our batch window is missing SLAs and some records are timing out at the client side.

We've attached a sample of the logs and a CPU/memory snapshot from our side. We turned down retries to a conservative exponential backoff but the problem persisted. Can you triage urgently? This is impacting our production ingestion and would appreciate an exec-level touch if needed.

Subject: Re: Severe p99 spikes + 429 cascade on fhir-batch during morning window

Taking this. Quick summary of what I'm seeing from our telemetry:

- Correlation between a spike in client-side retries (many concurrent short-interval retries) and an increase in request queuing on the fronting layer. The front-end rate limiter responded with 429s, which caused more client retries and higher queue length (classic retry amplification).
- p95/p99 regressions are amplified for requests with sequence lengths > 1024 tokens (these are common for some of Onyx's richer payloads during fhir-batch).
- Recent batching/config tweak (deployed 2026-07-19 03:12 UTC) altered our batching window heuristics for long-context requests; that appears to increase variance for tail latency under bursty retry traffic.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (order matters):
1) Enable per-customer concurrency cap (hard cap on concurrent in-flight requests) for Onyx to stop amplification.
2) Return Retry-After on excessive load and enforce exponential backoff guidance in a way that discourages tight client retries (we can also shift to 503 + Retry-After on overloaded frontends).
3) Short-term: route Onyx traffic to a dedicated, smaller-quantized model variant for requests > 1k tokens to reduce GPU tail latency.
4) Revert the batching-window tweak for long-context until we validate under retry noise.

I'll push a short debug snapshot to the ticket and attach the p95/p99 charts. ETA: can enact (1)+(2) within ~20 minutes if infra gives the green light.

-Rishi
Principal SW Eng, Serving Runtime

Confirming capacity pressure: our monitoring shows GPU pool 'hosted-prod-2' reached 92% utilization, and front-end connection churn increased ~4x starting at 09:43 PT. The batching heuristic change Rishi mentions did increase batching latency variance for long sequences; under steady load that's fine but with retries we see queueing.

Actions from Infra:
- I'll apply a per-customer concurrency shaper for Onyx (soft cap at 60 concurrent requests) and brief token-rate bump for 6 hours while we stabilize.
- If that doesn't drop queues within 15–30 minutes, we'll fall back to routing heavy sequences to a quantized fallback pool (may increase token-cost but reduce tail latency).
- We will keep logs for the incident and attach trace_snapshot_20260720.txt.

Note: we need an explicit customer agreement for temporary capacity bump and any credits/SLAs from billing.
